category: Views, Layouts, Plotting, File & Reference Management
description: Everything between finished geometry and issued output: how the drawing is looked at, how sheets and viewports are set up in paper space, how those sheets are plotted, published and exported, and how drawings are opened, cleaned, repaired, packaged and linked to external files. Almost all of it is scriptable from the command line, but most of these commands open a dialog unless FILEDIA is set to 0 or the hyphen-prefixed form is used.

tools.name: ZOOM
tools.description: Change the magnification of the current viewport without changing the drawing. Besides the familiar Window and Extents options it accepts a bare scale factor, where 2 means twice the drawing's real size, 2x means twice the current view, and 2xp means twice paper-space size. The nXP form is the only correct way to set the scale of a layout viewport, because it scales model geometry relative to paper units rather than to whatever happens to be on screen.
tools.usage:
ZOOM  (alias Z)
Specify corner of window, enter a scale factor (nX or nXP), or
[All/Center/Dynamic/Extents/Previous/Scale/Window/Object] <real time>:

parameters.name: All (A)
parameters.description: Display the whole of the drawing limits, or the extents if geometry falls outside the limits. Forces a regeneration.

parameters.name: Extents (E)
parameters.description: Display every object in the drawing as large as it will fit. Objects on frozen layers are ignored; a stray object miles from the origin is the usual reason ZOOM Extents looks wrong.

parameters.name: Center (C)
parameters.description: Give a centre point and then a magnification or a height in drawing units.

parameters.name: Window (W)
parameters.description: Zoom to a rectangle defined by two opposite corners. Picking two points without typing W does the same thing.

parameters.name: Previous (P)
parameters.description: Return to the previous view; up to ten views are remembered per viewport.

parameters.name: Scale (S) / nX / nXP
parameters.description: A plain number scales relative to the drawing limits, nX relative to the current view, and nXP relative to paper space units - so 1/50xp gives a 1:50 viewport in a millimetre drawing.

parameters.name: Object (O)
parameters.description: Select one or more objects and zoom so that they fill the viewport.

parameters.name: Dynamic (D)
parameters.description: Legacy option showing a pannable view box over the generated area; superseded by real-time zoom and pan.

tools.example:
; Set a layout viewport to exactly 1:50
MSPACE
ZOOM
1/50xp
PSPACE

; Fit everything on screen
ZOOM
E

; Zoom a known rectangle
ZOOM
W
0,0
1000,800

; AutoLISP
(command "_.ZOOM" "_E")
(command "_.ZOOM" "_S" "1/100xp")
tools.notes: Lock the viewport with the Properties palette or MVIEW Lock immediately after setting nXP scale, otherwise the next ZOOM inside the viewport silently destroys the scale. VIEWRES controls how smoothly circles and arcs are drawn on screen (it is a display setting only and never affects plotted output). Transparent use with a leading apostrophe ('ZOOM) works inside another command.

tools.name: PAN
tools.description: Shift the view without changing magnification. The normal form is an interactive real-time pan driven by the hand cursor, which is what the middle mouse button also does. Scripts and macros use the command-line form -PAN, which takes a base point and a second point and moves the view by that displacement.
tools.usage:
PAN  (alias P)
Press Esc or Enter to exit, or right-click to display shortcut menu.

; Command-line form used in scripts and macros
-PAN
Specify base point or displacement: <point>
Specify second point: <point>

parameters.name: base point / second point
parameters.description: In -PAN, the view moves by the vector between the two points. Entering a displacement and pressing Enter at the second prompt treats the first entry as the displacement.

parameters.name: real-time pan
parameters.description: Drag with the hand cursor; right-click for a shortcut menu offering Zoom, 3D Orbit and Exit.

parameters.name: middle button
parameters.description: MBUTTONPAN 1 (the default) makes press-and-drag on the wheel button pan without running the command.

parameters.name: transparent use
parameters.description: 'PAN can be run in the middle of another command, for example while picking a long dimension.

tools.example:
; Move the view 500 units to the right
-PAN
0,0
-500,0

; AutoLISP
(command "_.-PAN" '(0 0) '(-500 0))
tools.notes: PAN does not force a regeneration in most cases, but panning outside the generated area on a very large drawing can. Use ZOOM Previous to undo an accidental pan; PAN itself has no Undo option. The 3DPAN command is the equivalent in a perspective 3D view.

tools.name: VIEW
tools.description: Save, restore and manage named views: a stored combination of view centre, magnification, UCS, layer state, visual style and, for a layout view, the associated sheet. Named views are how repeated areas of a large drawing are reached instantly, how viewports are set to a known view with MVIEW Restore, and how sheet-set model views are defined. The dialog form is VIEW; scripts use -VIEW.
tools.usage:
VIEW  (alias V; dialog form, also DDVIEW)
(View Manager: Set Current / New / Update Layers / Edit Boundaries / Delete)

-VIEW
Enter an option [?/Delete/Orthographic/Restore/Save/sEttings/Window]: R | S | W | D | O | E | ?

parameters.name: Save (S)
parameters.description: Save the current display as a named view.

parameters.name: Restore (R)
parameters.description: Restore a named view into the current viewport.

parameters.name: Window (W)
parameters.description: Define a named view from a rectangle rather than from the current display.

parameters.name: Orthographic (O)
parameters.description: Restore one of the six preset orthographic views (Top, Bottom, Front, Back, Left, Right).

parameters.name: sEttings (E)
parameters.description: Control whether the view stores the current UCS, layer visibility, live section and visual style.

parameters.name: Delete (D) / ?
parameters.description: Delete a named view, or list the views defined in the drawing.

tools.example:
; Save the current display as a named view, then reuse it in a viewport
-VIEW
S
PLANT_AREA_3

; Later, in a layout viewport
MVIEW
50,50
250,200
MSPACE
-VIEW
R
PLANT_AREA_3
ZOOM
1/100xp
PSPACE
tools.notes: A named view saved with a layer state attached restores that layer state, which is a fast way to drive sheet content. Named views created in model space can be used by the Sheet Set Manager to place views on sheets. VIEWGO and VIEWPLAY animate a move to a named view; NAVSWHEEL and VIEWCUBE are the interactive alternatives.

tools.name: 3DORBIT
tools.description: Rotate the view in 3D around a target point while the model stays fixed. Constrained orbit (3DORBIT) keeps the Z axis vertical so the model never rolls over, free orbit (3DFORBIT) allows any rotation, and continuous orbit (3DCORBIT) keeps spinning after the drag is released. Use it to check a 3D model, not to change geometry - nothing in the drawing is modified.
tools.usage:
3DORBIT  (aliases 3DO, ORBIT)
Press Esc or Enter to exit, or right-click to display shortcut menu.

; Variants
3DFORBIT    free orbit (arcball)
3DCORBIT    continuous orbit

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: If objects are selected before the command starts, the orbit centres on that selection instead of the whole view.

parameters.name: ORBITAUTOTARGET
parameters.description: System variable: 1 (default) targets the objects being viewed, 0 targets the centre of the viewport.

parameters.name: PERSPECTIVE
parameters.description: System variable switching the current viewport between parallel (0) and perspective (1) projection.

parameters.name: shortcut menu
parameters.description: Right-click during the command to switch between Constrained, Free and Continuous orbit, Zoom, Pan, visual styles and preset views.

tools.example:
; Look at one assembly in isolation
ISOLATEOBJECTS
(select the assembly)

3DORBIT
(drag to the required angle, then press Esc)

; Store the result as a named view
-VIEW
S
ASSY_ISO

; Standard isometric without orbiting
-VIEW
R
SWISO
tools.notes: SHADEMODE and VSCURRENT set the visual style used while orbiting; wireframe orbits fastest on large models. Preset views SWISO, SEISO, NEISO, NWISO can be restored with -VIEW Restore and are usually quicker than orbiting by hand. Orbiting in a layout viewport changes that viewport's view, so lock the viewport first on finished sheets.

tools.name: REGEN
tools.description: Regenerate the drawing database for the current viewport and redraw it, recomputing the screen geometry of every visible object. It is needed after changing things that only take effect on regeneration - point styles, VIEWRES smoothness, FILLMODE, some linetype and text style changes - and it clears the display artefacts that occasionally survive a redraw. On very large drawings it is slow, which is why REGENAUTO exists.
tools.usage:
REGEN  (alias RE)
Regenerating model.

; Related
REGENAUTO <0|1>    automatic regeneration on or off
VIEWRES            circle and arc display smoothness

parameters.name: REGENAUTO
parameters.description: System variable: 1 lets AutoCAD regenerate whenever it needs to, 0 suppresses it and prompts instead. Set to 0 on huge drawings.

parameters.name: VIEWRES
parameters.description: Sets arc and circle display smoothness from 1 to 20000. It is a display setting only and never affects plotted output.

parameters.name: WHIPARC
parameters.description: System variable controlling whether circles and arcs are displayed as true curves (1) or as line segments (0).

parameters.name: REGENMODE
parameters.description: The system variable REGENAUTO is stored in REGENMODE; both report the same automatic regeneration setting.

tools.example:
; Points do not change appearance until a regen
PDMODE
34
PDSIZE
-3
REGEN

; Turn off fills for speed, then refresh
FILLMODE
0
REGEN
tools.notes: REDRAW only repaints the screen from the existing display list and is far cheaper than REGEN; try it first for stray pixels. REGENALL does the same as REGEN in every viewport at once. Changing a text style's font or a layer's linetype normally triggers a regeneration automatically unless REGENAUTO is 0.

tools.name: REGENALL
tools.description: Regenerate every viewport rather than only the current one, and redraw them all. It is the command to use after a change that affects several tiled model-space viewports or a layout with many floating viewports, for example altering a point style, a visual style, or a layer property that is overridden per viewport. In a single-viewport drawing it behaves exactly like REGEN.
tools.usage:
REGENALL  (alias REA)
Regenerating model.

; Compare
REGEN      current viewport only
REDRAWALL  repaint every viewport without recomputing

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: All viewports in the current space; it does not regenerate layouts that are not currently open.

parameters.name: REDRAWALL
parameters.description: Cheap alternative that repaints all viewports from the existing display list without recomputing geometry.

parameters.name: MAXACTVP
parameters.description: Maximum number of layout viewports that can be active (regenerated) at once, default 64; viewports beyond the limit go blank until activated.

tools.example:
; Refresh a whole sheet after changing viewport layer overrides
VPLAYER
F
GRID
A

REGENALL

; Cheaper refresh when only the screen is dirty
REDRAWALL
tools.notes: If a layout viewport shows nothing at all, check MAXACTVP before blaming the view: viewports over the limit are not regenerated. On drawings with heavy xrefs, REGENALL on a busy layout can take minutes; freeze unneeded layers per viewport with VPLAYER first.

tools.name: VSCURRENT
tools.description: Set the visual style of the current viewport: how edges, faces, shadows and background are displayed. 2D wireframe is the drafting default; Hidden, Realistic and Conceptual are the usual choices for checking a 3D model, and a viewport's visual style is also what the Shadeplot setting can send to the plotter. Each viewport carries its own visual style, so a layout can mix a shaded 3D view with a wireframe section.
tools.usage:
VSCURRENT  (alias VS)
Enter an option [2dwireframe/Wireframe/Hidden/Realistic/Conceptual/Shaded/shaded with Edges/
shades of Gray/SKetchy/X-ray/Other] <2dwireframe>:

; Manage and create styles
VISUALSTYLES   (alias VSM; command-line form -VISUALSTYLES)

parameters.name: 2dwireframe / Wireframe
parameters.description: Objects as lines and curves; 2D wireframe honours linetypes, lineweights and raster images, the 3D Wireframe style does not.

parameters.name: Hidden (H)
parameters.description: Wireframe with back faces removed - the classic hidden-line view for plotting 3D models.

parameters.name: Realistic / Conceptual
parameters.description: Smooth-shaded faces; Realistic uses materials, Conceptual uses the warm-cool Gooch shading that makes form easy to read.

parameters.name: Shaded / shaded with Edges
parameters.description: Flat shading without materials, optionally with the edges drawn on top.

parameters.name: Other (O)
parameters.description: Apply a custom visual style by name; custom styles are created and edited with VISUALSTYLES.

parameters.name: VSFACESTYLE / VSEDGES / VSSHADOWS
parameters.description: System variables behind the current style, controlling face shading mode, edge display mode and shadow display.

tools.example:
; Shade the 3D viewport on a sheet and plot it as displayed
MSPACE
VSCURRENT
C
PSPACE

; Hidden-line view for a general arrangement
VSCURRENT
H

; AutoLISP
(command "_.VSCURRENT" "_Hidden")
tools.notes: VISUALSTYLES (VSM) opens the Visual Styles Manager where custom styles are created; -VISUALSTYLES is its command-line form. SHADEMODE is the legacy command kept for scripts and maps onto the same styles. A viewport's plotted appearance is set by the Shade plot property (MVIEW Shadeplot or the Properties palette), which can differ from what is on screen.

tools.name: VPORTS
tools.description: Divide the drawing area into viewports. In model space (TILEMODE 1) it creates tiled viewport configurations that can be saved by name and restored later, which is how a 3D model is worked on in plan, front and isometric at once. In a layout (TILEMODE 0) it creates floating layout viewports, including named configurations restored from model space, and the command-line form -VPORTS is what scripts use.
tools.usage:
VPORTS  (dialog; command-line form -VPORTS)

; Model space
-VPORTS
Enter an option [Save/Restore/Delete/Join/SIngle/?/2/3/4/Toggle/MOde] <3>:

; In a layout, -VPORTS offers the floating-viewport options
[ON/OFF/Fit/Shadeplot/Lock/Object/Polygonal/Restore/LAyer/2/3/4]

parameters.description: Split into two, three or four viewports, then choose the arrangement (Horizontal, Vertical, Above, Below, Left, Right).

parameters.name: Save (S) / Restore (R)
parameters.description: Store the current tiled arrangement under a name and bring it back later, including in a layout.

parameters.name: SIngle (SI)
parameters.description: Collapse back to one viewport showing the current one.

parameters.name: Join (J)
parameters.description: Merge two adjacent tiled viewports into one rectangle.

parameters.name: CVPORT
parameters.description: System variable holding the identifier of the current viewport; useful in LISP that must act on a particular viewport.

parameters.name: TILEMODE
parameters.description: 1 puts you in model space with tiled viewports, 0 in a layout with floating viewports. LAYOUT, MSPACE and PSPACE set it for you.

parameters.name: MAXACTVP
parameters.description: Maximum number of layout viewports regenerated at once, default 64.

tools.example:
; Three model-space viewports, saved for reuse
-VPORTS
3
R
-VPORTS
S
MODEL_3UP

; Restore that arrangement as floating viewports on a sheet
LAYOUT
S
A1 - GA
-VPORTS
R
MODEL_3UP
0,0
800,550
tools.notes: Tiled model-space viewports are a working aid and are never plotted; only layout viewports appear in output. MVIEW is the more direct command for creating individual floating viewports, and VPCLIP reshapes one. Put layout viewport borders on a dedicated non-plotting layer so the rectangles never print.

tools.name: LAYOUT
tools.description: Create, copy, rename, delete and switch layouts, and import a layout from a drawing or template file. Every layout is a sheet of paper with its own page setup, its own viewports and its own paper-space geometry. Because LAYOUT is a pure command-line command it is the backbone of scripted sheet production, where a template layout is imported into many drawings and then plotted.
tools.usage:
LAYOUT  (alias LO)
Enter layout option [Copy/Delete/New/Template/Rename/SAveas/Set/?] <set>:

; Examples of each
LAYOUT N <name>          create a new empty layout
LAYOUT T <file.dwt>      import a layout from a template or drawing
LAYOUT S <name>          make a layout current
LAYOUT SA <name> <file>  save a layout out as a template

parameters.name: New (N)
parameters.description: Create a new empty layout with the given name; a default viewport may be created depending on the page setup.

parameters.name: Template (T)
parameters.description: Import a layout, with its page setup and paper-space content, from a DWT, DWG or DXF file. The workhorse option for standardising sheets.

parameters.name: Copy (C) / Rename (R) / Delete (D)
parameters.description: Duplicate, rename or remove a layout. At least one layout must always remain.

parameters.name: SAveas (SA)
parameters.description: Write the current layout out to a drawing template file so other drawings can import it.

parameters.name: Set (S)
parameters.description: Make the named layout current, which is what -PLOT and PAGESETUP then act on.

parameters.name: CTAB
parameters.description: System variable holding the name of the current layout or tab ("Model" in model space); read it in LISP to loop over sheets.

tools.example:
; Import the office A1 sheet, then set it current
FILEDIA 0
LAYOUT
T
C:/standards/templates/A1_SHEET.dwt
A1 - GA
LAYOUT
S
A1 - GA

; AutoLISP: plot every layout in the drawing
(foreach lay (layoutlist)
  (setvar "CTAB" lay)
  (princ (strcat "\nCurrent layout: " lay)))
tools.notes: Set FILEDIA 0 before LAYOUT Template in a script or the template file dialog stops it. The (layoutlist) LISP function returns every layout name except Model, which is the normal way to drive batch plotting. LAYOUTWIZARD walks through creating a layout interactively but is not scriptable; PAGESETUP is the command that assigns a device and paper size to the finished layout.

tools.name: MVIEW
tools.description: Create and control floating viewports in a layout: the windows through which model space is seen on a sheet. Viewports can be rectangular, polygonal, or made from an existing closed object, and each one can be turned off, locked, given its own shade plot setting and its own layer visibility. It only works in paper space, so run PSPACE or LAYOUT first.
tools.usage:
MVIEW  (alias MV)
Specify corner of viewport or
[ON/OFF/Fit/Shadeplot/Lock/New/NAmed/Object/Polygonal/Restore/LAyer/2/3/4] <Fit>:
Specify opposite corner:

parameters.name: Fit (F)
parameters.description: Create one viewport filling the printable area of the sheet.

parameters.name: Object (O)
parameters.description: Turn an existing closed polyline, circle, ellipse, spline or region into the viewport boundary - the way non-rectangular details are made.

parameters.name: Polygonal (P)
parameters.description: Draw an irregular viewport boundary from line and arc segments.

parameters.name: ON / OFF
parameters.description: Switch a viewport's model display on or off. Turning unused viewports off is the quickest cure for a slow sheet.

parameters.name: Lock (L)
parameters.description: Lock a viewport's zoom scale so that zooming inside it pans the view instead of rescaling it. Do this the moment the nXP scale is right.

parameters.name: Shadeplot (S)
parameters.description: How the viewport plots: As Displayed, Wireframe, Hidden, Visual Styles or Rendered - independent of what is on screen.
Create two, three or four viewports at once inside a picked rectangle or fitted to the sheet.

parameters.name: Restore (R)
parameters.description: Create floating viewports from a named model-space viewport configuration saved with VPORTS.

tools.example:
; Sheet with a main view at 1:100 and a locked detail at 1:20
LAYOUT
S
A1 - GA
PSPACE
-LAYER M VIEWPORTS P N VIEWPORTS

MVIEW
20,20
560,380
MSPACE
ZOOM
1/100xp
PSPACE
MVIEW
L
ON
L


MVIEW
600,250
800,380
MSPACE
ZOOM
1/20xp
PSPACE
tools.notes: Put all viewport boundaries on one non-plotting layer so the rectangles never appear in output. MSPACE enters the viewport under the cursor and PSPACE returns to the sheet; double-clicking inside or outside a viewport does the same. VPCLIP reshapes an existing viewport, and VPLAYER freezes layers in one viewport only. MAXACTVP caps how many viewports are regenerated at once.

tools.name: MSPACE
tools.description: Switch from paper space into model space inside a floating viewport, so that pans, zooms, views and model geometry are edited through that window. It only works when a layout is current (TILEMODE 0) and at least one viewport is on. It is the half of the paper-space workflow that sets viewport views and scales; PSPACE is the other half.
tools.usage:
MSPACE  (alias MS)
; Requires TILEMODE = 0 and an active viewport.
; Double-clicking inside a viewport does the same thing.

parameters.name: TILEMODE
parameters.description: Must be 0 (a layout current). In model space MSPACE reports that the command is not available.

parameters.name: CVPORT
parameters.description: Identifies which viewport becomes active; set it in LISP to choose a viewport before zooming.

parameters.name: current viewport
parameters.description: MSPACE activates the last active viewport; click in another viewport to switch, or press Ctrl+R to cycle.

tools.example:
; Set a viewport to 1:200 and freeze a layer in it only
MSPACE
ZOOM
1/200xp
VPLAYER
F
SURVEY_GRID


PSPACE
tools.notes: Editing model geometry from inside a viewport is real editing - it changes the model, not the sheet. Lock the viewport (MVIEW Lock ON) once the scale is correct so that a stray zoom cannot rescale it; a locked viewport still allows panning and object editing.

tools.name: PSPACE
tools.description: Return from model space inside a viewport to paper space, where the sheet itself is edited: title block, notes, viewport borders, dimensions that belong to the sheet rather than the model. Only available when a layout is current. Anything drawn while in paper space lives on that layout alone and is invisible from model space.
tools.usage:
PSPACE  (alias PS)
; Requires TILEMODE = 0.
; Double-clicking outside every viewport does the same thing.

parameters.name: TILEMODE
parameters.description: Must be 0. Use LAYOUT Set or click a layout tab first.

parameters.name: paper units
parameters.description: In paper space, one drawing unit is one paper unit (normally one millimetre or one inch), so title blocks are drawn at full size.

parameters.name: PSLTSCALE
parameters.description: System variable: 1 (default) scales linetypes in viewports to paper space so dashes look the same at every viewport scale.

parameters.name: ANNOALLVISIBLE / annotative scale
parameters.description: Annotative text and dimensions size themselves from the viewport's annotation scale, which is the alternative to drawing notes in paper space.

tools.example:
; Add a sheet note and a title block in paper space
PSPACE
-INSERT
TITLEBLOCK_A1
0,0
1
1
0
-MTEXT
20,560
H
3.5
J
TL
W
120
GENERAL ARRANGEMENT - DO NOT SCALE
tools.notes: Keep dimensions in the space that owns the geometry: paper-space dimensions attached to model objects through a viewport break when the viewport is panned or rescaled. PSLTSCALE 1 with a REGENALL fixes linetype dashes that look wrong at different viewport scales.

tools.name: VPLAYER
tools.description: Control layer visibility and property overrides viewport by viewport, so the same model can show different content in each window on a sheet. Freezing a layer with VPLAYER affects only the chosen viewports, unlike LAYER Freeze which affects the whole drawing. Newer releases add per-viewport colour, linetype, lineweight and transparency overrides through the same command.
tools.usage:
VPLAYER
Enter an option [?/Color/LType/LWeight/TRansparency/Freeze/Thaw/Reset/Newfrz/Vpvisdflt]:
Enter layer name(s) to freeze: <names>
Enter an option [All/Select/Current] <Current>: A | S | C

parameters.name: Freeze (F) / Thaw (T)
parameters.description: Freeze or thaw named layers in the chosen viewports only; wildcards such as X-* are accepted.

parameters.name: All / Select / Current
parameters.description: Which viewports the change applies to: every viewport, ones you pick, or just the current one.

parameters.name: Reset (R)
parameters.description: Return the named layers in the chosen viewports to their default visibility, discarding the per-viewport setting.

parameters.name: Newfrz (N)
parameters.description: Create new layers that are frozen in all viewports - handy for content that should be opted into rather than out of.

parameters.name: Vpvisdflt (V)
parameters.description: Set the default viewport visibility for a layer, which decides whether it is visible in viewports created afterwards.

parameters.name: Color / LType / LWeight / TRansparency
parameters.description: Per-viewport property overrides, shown in the Layer Properties Manager's VP columns and highlighted so they are easy to spot.

parameters.name: VISRETAIN
parameters.description: System variable deciding whether layer settings you make for xref-dependent layers survive a reload; 1 keeps them.

tools.example:
; Hide the survey grid in every viewport except the current one
MSPACE
VPLAYER
F
SURVEY_GRID
A

VPLAYER
T
SURVEY_GRID
C

PSPACE
REGENALL
tools.notes: Per-viewport freezing is stored on the viewport, so copying a viewport copies its overrides. The Layer Properties Manager shows the same settings in the VP Freeze and VP colour columns when a layout is current. LAYERSTATE saves and restores whole sets of layer settings, which scales better than long VPLAYER lists.

tools.name: PAGESETUP
tools.description: Open the Page Setup Manager, where each layout is given its output device, paper size, plot area, scale, plot style table and drawing orientation. A named page setup can be saved in the drawing and imported from another drawing or template, which is how an office applies identical plot settings to every sheet. What PLOT and PUBLISH do by default is exactly what the page setup says.
tools.usage:
PAGESETUP
(Page Setup Manager: Set Current / New / Modify / Import)
(Page Setup dialog: Printer/plotter, Paper size, Plot area, Plot offset,
 Plot scale, Plot style table, Shaded viewport options, Plot options, Drawing orientation)

parameters.name: Printer/plotter
parameters.description: A system printer or a .pc3 configuration such as DWG To PDF.pc3, created with PLOTTERMANAGER.

parameters.name: Paper size
parameters.description: Comes from the selected device; a full-bleed size is needed when the sheet border must reach the paper edge.

parameters.name: Plot area
parameters.description: Layout, Extents, Display, View, Window or Limits. For a sheet, Layout is normally correct.

parameters.name: Plot scale
parameters.description: 1:1 for a layout (the viewports carry the model scale); Fit to paper is for quick check prints only.

parameters.name: Plot style table
parameters.description: A .ctb (colour-dependent) or .stb (named) table controlling plotted colour, lineweight and screening.

parameters.name: Shaded viewport options
parameters.description: Shade plot mode and output DPI for viewports containing shaded 3D views.

parameters.name: Import
parameters.description: Pull a named page setup in from another DWG, DWT or DXF, which is how standards are rolled out across sheets.

parameters.name: PSTYLEMODE / PSTYLEPOLICY
parameters.description: Whether the drawing uses colour-dependent or named plot styles; a drawing cannot mix the two, and CONVERTPSTYLES switches it.

tools.example:
; Typical sequence when preparing a sheet
LAYOUT
S
A1 - GA
PAGESETUP
(Import the office setup "A1-PDF-MONO" from C:/standards/templates/A1_SHEET.dwt)
(Set Current, then Close)
PREVIEW
tools.notes: -PLOT can override any of these settings sheet by sheet and optionally write the result back with its Save changes to page setup prompt. A named page setup is also what PUBLISH uses when a sheet's page setup column is set to something other than <Default: none>. LAYOUTWIZARD creates a layout and its page setup together but cannot be scripted.

tools.name: VPCLIP
tools.description: Clip an existing layout viewport to a new boundary, or delete an existing clip to restore the rectangle. The boundary can be an existing closed object - circle, ellipse, closed polyline, spline or region - or drawn on the spot as a polygon. It is how round detail bubbles and irregular site-plan windows are made without deleting and recreating the viewport.
tools.usage:
VPCLIP
Select viewport to clip: <viewport border>

Answering Yes at the first prompt gives the full detailed sequence below; answering No gives a short sequence that uses the layout's page setup for everything else.

The prompts differ slightly between releases and between devices - a device that can only write to a file skips the Write-to-file question and goes straight to the file name - so record one run interactively and copy the exact answers. PLOTSTAMP adds a plot stamp, PREVIEW shows the result first, and PUBLISH is the better tool for many sheets at once.

tools.name: PREVIEW
tools.description: Display the current layout or plot area exactly as it will come out of the plotter, using the assigned device, paper size, plot style table and lineweights. It is the fastest way to catch a wrong plot style table, a viewport that is off, lineweights that are far too heavy, or content falling outside the printable area. Press Esc or right-click to leave the preview.
tools.usage:
PREVIEW  (alias PRE)
; Displays a full plot preview of the current layout using its page setup.
; Right-click for Plot, Pan, Zoom, Zoom Original and Exit; Esc closes the preview.

parameters.name: page setup
parameters.description: The preview uses the current layout's page setup, so change it with PAGESETUP rather than inside the preview.

parameters.name: plot style table
parameters.description: The preview honours the assigned .ctb or .stb, which is how a monochrome plot is verified before paper is used.

parameters.name: LWDISPLAY
parameters.description: Controls lineweight display in the editor, not in the preview - the preview always shows plotted lineweights.

parameters.name: printable area
parameters.description: The dashed margin shown in the layout; anything outside it is clipped, which the preview makes obvious.

tools.example:
LAYOUT
S
A1 - GA
PAGESETUP
(check device, paper size and plot style table)
PREVIEW
(Esc to return, then plot)
PLOT
tools.notes: A preview that comes out blank almost always means the plot area is set to Limits or Extents in a layout with nothing in model space, or a viewport that has been turned off with MVIEW OFF. The plot dialog has its own preview button that does the same thing. Hidden or shaded viewports render in the preview, which can make it slow on large 3D sheets.

tools.name: PUBLISH
tools.description: Plot a list of sheets from one or many drawings in a single operation, to plotters, to a multi-sheet PDF or DWF/DWFx, or to each sheet's own page setup. The sheet list can be built by hand, loaded from an open drawing set, or taken from the Sheet Set Manager, and it can be saved as a .dsd drawing set description for reuse. It is the right tool for issuing a whole drawing package.
tools.usage:
PUBLISH
(Publish dialog: sheet list, Publish to: Plotter named in page setup | DWF | DWFx | PDF,
 Publish Options, Number of copies, Precision, Include plot stamp, Publish in background)

; Command-line form driven by a saved sheet list
-PUBLISH
Enter the DSD file name: <path\sheets.dsd>

parameters.name: Publish to
parameters.description: The plotter named in each sheet's page setup, or a single multi-sheet DWF, DWFx or PDF file.

parameters.name: Page setup column
parameters.description: Each sheet can be overridden with a named page setup imported into the list, which is how mixed paper sizes are handled.

parameters.name: Publish Options
parameters.description: Output location, single-sheet or multi-sheet file, naming, layer information, and whether the DWF/PDF is password protected.

parameters.name: Include plot stamp
parameters.description: Adds the PLOTSTAMP information to each sheet as it is published.

parameters.name: PUBLISHCOLLATE
parameters.description: System variable: 1 keeps a publish job together as one plot job so other plots cannot interleave with it.

parameters.name: BACKGROUNDPLOT
parameters.description: Controls background publishing; set to 0 when a script must wait for the job to finish.

parameters.name: .dsd file
parameters.description: The saved drawing set description listing drawings, layouts and page setups; -PUBLISH takes one as its only argument.

tools.example:
; Publish a saved sheet list from a script

BACKGROUNDPLOT
0
-PUBLISH
C:/plot/1042_ISSUE_C.dsd

; Interactive: build the list, then save it for next time

(add sheets, set Publish to: PDF, Save Sheet List as 1042_ISSUE_C.dsd)
tools.notes: -PUBLISH cannot build a sheet list; it only replays a .dsd created in the dialog or by the Sheet Set Manager, so save the list once and script the rest. BATCHPLOT is not a core AutoCAD command - use PUBLISH, a .dsd file, or the Sheet Set Manager's Publish option for batch output. Background publishing returns control immediately, so set BACKGROUNDPLOT to 0 before scripting it or the drawing may close mid-job.

tools.name: EXPORT
tools.description: Save the drawing, or a selection from it, in another file format. It is the single entry point for the vector and model exchange formats AutoCAD supports - DWF, DWFx, PDF, WMF, SAT, STL, EPS, DXX, BMP, DGN and IGES among them - with the format chosen by the file type in the Save As dialog. The command-line form -EXPORT takes the format and file name at the prompt so it can be scripted.
tools.usage:
EXPORT  (alias EXP; command-line form -EXPORT)
(Export Data dialog: file name and Files of type)

-EXPORT
Enter file format [Dwf/dwfX/Pdf/Wmf/Sat/Stl/Eps/Dxx/Bmp/Dgn/Iges/IGEs]: <format>
Enter file name <drawing.ext>: <path>
(then format-specific prompts and object selection)

parameters.name: Dwf / dwfX
parameters.description: Design Web Format for review and issue; keeps layers and object data and is far smaller than a DWG.

parameters.name: Pdf
parameters.description: PDF output; EXPORTPDF exposes the same engine with its presets and options.

parameters.name: Sat
parameters.description: ACIS solid model text file, the usual exchange format for 3D solids into other modellers.

parameters.name: Stl
parameters.description: Stereolithography mesh of selected solids, for 3D printing. Solids must be positioned entirely in positive XYZ space.

parameters.name: Wmf / Eps / Bmp
parameters.description: Windows metafile, encapsulated PostScript and bitmap output for placing drawings in other documents.

parameters.name: Dgn
parameters.description: MicroStation DGN export, with a mapping setup that controls how layers become levels.

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: Must be 0 for -EXPORT in a script, otherwise the Export Data dialog appears.

tools.example:

C:/out/bracket.stl
(select the 3D solids)

DXFOUT writes DXF and SAVEAS with the DXF option does the same. For batch PDF or DWF of many sheets use PUBLISH rather than repeated EXPORT calls.

tools.name: EXPORTPDF
tools.description: Export the current layout, the display, the extents or a picked window to a PDF file using a PDF preset. Unlike plotting through the DWG To PDF.pc3 driver it exposes the export options directly - layer information, hyperlinks, bookmarks, whether SHX text is searchable, and the vector and raster resolution. It is the quickest route from one sheet to a clean PDF.

  Export: Current layout | Display | Extents | Window

parameters.name: PDF Preset
parameters.description: A .pc3-backed preset trading quality against file size; General Documentation is the everyday choice.

parameters.name: Export
parameters.description: Current layout, Display, Extents or a picked Window - the same choices as the plot area.

parameters.name: Page Setup: Override
parameters.description: Change paper size, plot style table and orientation for this export without editing the layout's page setup.

parameters.name: Include layer information
parameters.description: Writes AutoCAD layers into the PDF so the reader can switch them on and off.

parameters.name: PDFSHX
parameters.description: System variable: 1 stores SHX text as searchable comment data in the PDF, 0 exports it as plain geometry.

parameters.name: Create bookmarks
parameters.description: Adds PDF bookmarks from layout names and named views, useful in multi-sheet output.

parameters.name: vector / raster resolution
parameters.description: DPI for vector geometry and for embedded images; raising it enlarges the file quickly.

tools.name: EXPORTDWF
tools.description: Export the current layout, display, extents or a window to a DWF file, the compact Autodesk review format that keeps layers, named views and block attribute data. DWF is what a design team issues for markup and viewing when a PDF is too flat and a DWG gives away too much. EXPORTDWFX produces the newer XPS-based DWFx, which opens in Windows without a separate viewer.
tools.usage:
EXPORTDWF   (Save As DWF dialog)
EXPORTDWFX (Save As DWFx dialog)
  Export: Current layout | Display | Extents | Window
  Page Setup: Current | Override
  Options: password protection, block information, block template file, layer information

parameters.name: Export
parameters.description: Current layout, Display, Extents or a picked Window.

parameters.name: Page Setup: Override
parameters.description: Apply a different paper size, orientation or plot style table for this export only.

parameters.name: Include layer information
parameters.description: Keeps layers switchable in the DWF viewer.

parameters.name: Block information / block template
parameters.description: Publishes block attribute data into the DWF, optionally filtered by a .blk template, so the viewer can query properties.

parameters.name: Password protection
parameters.description: Encrypts the DWF; a lost password cannot be recovered.

parameters.name: DWFFRAME

tools.example:

S
A1 - GA
EXPORTDWF
(Export: Current layout, file C:/issue/1042-A1-GA.dwf)

(add sheets, Publish to: DWF, multi-sheet file C:/issue/1042_ISSUE_C.dwf)

tools.name: PLOTTERMANAGER
tools.description: Open the Plotters window, which holds the .pc3 plotter configuration files this installation can plot to, and launches the Add-A-Plotter wizard to create new ones. A .pc3 file stores the device, its driver settings, custom paper sizes, calibration and the default output folder, so it is how an office standardises on names such as DWG To PDF.pc3 or A1 Plotter.pc3. Double-click an existing .pc3 to edit it in the Plotter Configuration Editor.
tools.usage:
PLOTTERMANAGER
(Plotters window: Add-A-Plotter Wizard, existing .pc3 files)
(Plotter Configuration Editor: General / Ports / Device and Document Settings)
  Device and Document Settings -> Custom Paper Sizes, Modify Standard Paper Sizes,

parameters.name: Custom Paper Sizes
parameters.description: Define non-standard sheet sizes and their printable margins - the usual fix for a border that will not fit.

parameters.name: Modify Standard Paper Sizes

parameters.name: Ports

parameters.name: Custom Properties

parameters.name: PRINTERCONFIGDIR

STYLESMANAGER is the companion command for plot style tables. Custom paper sizes live inside the .pc3 and travel with it, which is why a sheet that plots correctly on one machine can fail on another.

tools.name: STYLESMANAGER
tools.description: Open the Plot Styles folder, which holds the plot style tables that map drawing objects to plotted colour, lineweight, screening, line end and join styles, and launches the Add-A-Plot-Style-Table wizard. Colour-dependent tables (.ctb) key off the object's colour, which is the traditional pen-table workflow; named tables (.stb) assign styles to objects and layers explicitly. Double-click a table to edit it in the Plot Style Table Editor.

(Plot Styles folder: Add-A-Plot-Style-Table Wizard, existing .ctb and .stb files)
(Plot Style Table Editor: General / Table View / Form View)
  per style: Color, Dither, Grayscale, Pen #, Virtual pen #, Screening,

parameters.name: .stb (named)

parameters.name: Lineweight

parameters.name: CONVERTPSTYLES
parameters.description: Command that converts the current drawing between colour-dependent and named plot styles; a drawing cannot use both.

parameters.name: CONVERTCTB
parameters.description: Command that converts an existing .ctb file into a .stb file so a named-style workflow can reuse the old pen settings.
