tools.name: OPEN
tools.description: Open an existing drawing, DXF, DWS standards file or DWT template. Interactively it shows the Select File dialog with options to open read-only, partially open by view and layer, or open selected sheets from a sheet set. In scripts it must be preceded by FILEDIA 0, which turns it into a plain command-line prompt for the file name - the foundation of every batch-processing script.
tools.usage:
OPEN
(Select File dialog: Open | Open Read-Only | Partial Open | Partial Open Read-Only)

; Scripted form
FILEDIA 0
OPEN
Enter name of drawing to open: <full path>

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: Must be 0 for a scripted open. Restore it to 1 afterwards or the interactive session is left without file dialogs.

parameters.name: Read-only
parameters.description: Opens without a lock so the file can be inspected while someone else edits it; SAVEAS is then needed to keep changes.

parameters.name: Partial Open
parameters.description: Loads only selected views and layers from a very large drawing; PARTIALOAD brings in more geometry later.

parameters.name: SDI
parameters.description: System variable: 1 forces single-document mode, which older batch scripts rely on so that OPEN replaces the current drawing rather than adding a tab.

parameters.name: RECOVERYMODE / DWGCHECK
parameters.description: Control what happens when a damaged drawing is opened; DWGCHECK warns about files not produced by Autodesk software.

parameters.name: unsaved changes
parameters.description: If the current drawing is modified, OPEN prompts to save; answer it in the script or run QSAVE first.

tools.example:
; Batch script: open, purge, save, next
FILEDIA 0
SDI 1
OPEN
C:/jobs/1042/1042-100.dwg
-PURGE
All
*
N
QSAVE
OPEN
C:/jobs/1042/1042-101.dwg
-PURGE
All
*
N
QSAVE
FILEDIA 1
tools.notes: CLOSE closes the current drawing, CLOSEALL closes every open drawing and QUIT exits the program - all three ask about unsaved changes unless the drawing is already saved. NEW and QNEW create a new drawing (QNEW uses the default template set in OPTIONS and skips the template dialog, which is what makes it scriptable). RECOVER is the command to use instead of OPEN when a drawing is damaged.

tools.name: QSAVE
tools.description: Save the current drawing under its existing name and format without any prompt, which is what Ctrl+S does. If the drawing has never been saved it behaves like SAVEAS and asks for a name, so a batch script should always know whether the file is titled. It is the safe save to put at the end of each loop in a batch script because it never changes the file name or the DWG version.
tools.usage:
QSAVE
; No prompts when the drawing already has a name.
; If untitled, the Save Drawing As dialog appears (or a command-line prompt when FILEDIA is 0).

parameters.name: DWGTITLED
parameters.description: System variable: 0 means the drawing has never been named, so QSAVE will prompt. Test it in LISP before saving in a batch.

parameters.name: DBMOD
parameters.description: Bit-coded system variable reporting what has been modified since the last save; 0 means there is nothing to save.

parameters.name: SAVETIME
parameters.description: Automatic save interval in minutes; 0 disables it. Automatic saves write a .sv$ file, they do not update the DWG.

parameters.name: ISAVEPERCENT
parameters.description: Percentage of wasted space tolerated in a DWG before a full save is forced instead of an incremental one.

parameters.name: read-only
parameters.description: QSAVE fails on a drawing opened read-only; use SAVEAS to write it elsewhere.

tools.example:
; Save only if something changed
(if (/= 0 (getvar "DBMOD"))
  (command "_.QSAVE")
  (princ "\nNothing to save."))

; In a script
QSAVE
CLOSE
tools.notes: SAVE (as opposed to QSAVE) always prompts for a file name and saves to it without making that file current, which surprises people expecting QSAVE behaviour. QSAVE keeps the format the file already has; use SAVEAS to change DWG version. Set SAVETIME to a sensible 10 to 15 minutes - the .sv$ file is what DRAWINGRECOVERY offers after a crash.

tools.name: SAVEAS
tools.description: Save the current drawing under a new name, a new location or a different file format, and make that new file the current drawing. It is how a drawing is downsaved to an older DWG version for a consultant, written out as DXF, or turned into a DWT template or DWS standards file. With FILEDIA set to 0 it becomes a command-line sequence and can be scripted.
tools.usage:
SAVEAS
(Save Drawing As dialog: File name, Files of type - DWG versions, DXF, DWT, DWS)

; Scripted form
FILEDIA 0
SAVEAS
Enter file format [...list of supported DWG versions.../DXF/Template/Options] <current>: <format> | Enter
Save drawing as <current name>: <full path>

parameters.name: file format
parameters.description: The DWG release to write, or DXF, Template (.dwt) or Standards (.dws). The exact list of releases depends on the AutoCAD version in use.

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: Set to 0 before scripting SAVEAS so the prompts appear at the command line.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description: In the dialog, sets DXF precision, thumbnail preview and whether a backup is created.

parameters.name: existing file
parameters.description: Saving over an existing file prompts for confirmation; answer the prompt in the script or the script stalls.

parameters.name: ISAVEBAK / SAVEFILEPATH
parameters.description: Whether a .bak backup is written, and where automatic saves are placed.

parameters.name: DWGPREFIX / DWGNAME
parameters.description: Read-only system variables giving the current drawing's folder and file name; use them to build the new path in LISP.

tools.example:
; Downsave a whole folder to an older DWG release
FILEDIA 0
OPEN
C:/jobs/1042/1042-100.dwg
SAVEAS
2013
C:/issue/2013/1042-100.dwg
OPEN
C:/jobs/1042/1042-101.dwg
SAVEAS
2013
C:/issue/2013/1042-101.dwg
FILEDIA 1

; AutoLISP: save a copy beside the original
(command "_.SAVEAS" "" (strcat (getvar "DWGPREFIX") "COPY_" (getvar "DWGNAME")))
tools.notes: SAVEAS switches the editing session to the new file, so subsequent edits do not touch the original - use WBLOCK or a file copy when the original must stay current. Downsaving loses objects that the older format does not support, which is why a downsaved file should always be reopened and checked. ETRANSMIT is the better tool when a consultant needs the xrefs and fonts as well.

tools.name: PURGE
tools.description: Remove unused named objects from the drawing - block definitions, layers, linetypes, text and dimension styles, materials, plot styles, table and multileader styles - along with registered applications, zero-length geometry, empty text objects and orphaned data. It is the first step in cleaning a bloated file and is normally run several times because purging one item can free another. The command-line form -PURGE is the one scripts use.
tools.usage:
PURGE  (alias PU)
(dialog: Purgeable Items / Find Non-Purgeable Items, Purge nested items,
         Purge zero-length geometry and empty text objects, Automatically purge orphaned data)

-PURGE
Enter type of unused objects to purge
[Blocks/DEtailviewstyles/Dimstyles/Groups/LAyers/LTypes/MAterials/MUltileaderstyles/
 Plotstyles/SHapes/textSTyles/Mlinestyles/SEctionviewstyles/Tablestyles/Visualstyles/
 Regapps/Zero-length geometry/Empty text objects/Orphaned data/All]: All
Enter name(s) to purge <*>: *
Verify each name to be purged? [Yes/No] <Y>: N

parameters.name: All
parameters.description: Purge every purgeable type. With name * and verify N this is the standard scripted cleanup: -PURGE All * N.

parameters.name: Regapps
parameters.description: Registered application names left behind by third-party software and extended entity data; a common source of silent file growth.

parameters.name: Zero-length geometry
parameters.description: Lines, arcs and polylines of no length that are invisible but still selected and still plotted as dots.

parameters.name: Orphaned data
parameters.description: Dictionary entries and extension data no longer referenced by anything in the drawing.

parameters.name: Purge nested items
parameters.description: Purges blocks that are only referenced by other unused blocks; without it, several passes are needed.

parameters.name: name(s) to purge
parameters.description: Wildcards accepted; * purges everything of the chosen type. Named items still in use are never purged.

parameters.name: Verify
parameters.description: Yes asks about each item individually. Always answer N in scripts or the script stops on the first question.

tools.example:
; Scripted cleanup, run twice to catch nested definitions
-PURGE
All
*
N
-PURGE
All
*
N
AUDIT
Y
QSAVE

; AutoLISP
(command "_.-PURGE" "_All" "*" "_N")
tools.notes: Layer 0, the DEFPOINTS layer, the current layer, the STANDARD text and dimension styles and the CONTINUOUS linetype can never be purged. A layer that will not purge usually still holds an object inside a block definition or an unreferenced xref - use the dialog's Find Non-Purgeable Items to see why. WBLOCK with the Entire drawing option is the heavier cleanup that rebuilds the file from referenced objects only; OVERKILL removes duplicate geometry that PURGE cannot see.

tools.name: AUDIT
tools.description: Check the current drawing's database for structural errors and optionally fix them. It reports the number of errors found and corrected, and with AUDITCTL on it writes an .adt log next to the drawing listing what it did. Run it on any file that behaves strangely - commands failing for no reason, objects that cannot be selected, unexplained file growth - and always before issuing a drawing.
tools.usage:
AUDIT
Fix any errors detected? [Yes/No] <N>: Y
(Auditing Header / Tables / Entities / Blocks / Objects)
Total errors found n, fixed n.

parameters.name: Fix any errors detected
parameters.description: Yes repairs what it can; No reports only. In scripts always answer explicitly.

parameters.name: AUDITCTL
parameters.description: System variable: 1 writes an .adt audit log beside the drawing, 0 (default) does not.

parameters.name: DWGCHECK
parameters.description: Controls whether opening a drawing that is damaged or not produced by an Autodesk product raises a warning.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: AUDIT works on the drawing already open; a file too damaged to open needs RECOVER instead.

tools.example:
; Clean and check every drawing in a batch
FILEDIA 0
AUDITCTL 1
OPEN
C:/jobs/1042/1042-100.dwg
AUDIT
Y
-PURGE
All
*
N
QSAVE
FILEDIA 1
tools.notes: AUDIT cannot repair a file that will not open - that is what RECOVER is for, and RECOVERALL does the same for the drawing plus all of its attached xrefs. A drawing that reports errors on every audit is usually being corrupted by a third-party application or a network problem; WBLOCK of the entire drawing into a fresh file often clears what AUDIT cannot. DRAWINGRECOVERY opens the Drawing Recovery Manager after a crash, offering the .dwg, .bak and .sv$ versions side by side.

tools.name: RECOVER
tools.description: Open a damaged drawing or DXF file and run an audit on it as it is opened, repairing what it can. Use it when OPEN fails, when AutoCAD reports that a drawing is not valid, or when a file opens but behaves as if the database is corrupt. It works on a file that is not currently open, so it is the entry point for a rescue rather than a maintenance command.
tools.usage:
RECOVER
(Select File dialog - or a command-line prompt when FILEDIA is 0)
Enter name of drawing file to recover: <full path>
(Drawing recovery log appears in the text window)

; Related
RECOVERALL   recover the drawing and every attached xref
DRAWINGRECOVERY   Drawing Recovery Manager after a crash

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: A DWG or DXF file. It is opened as the current drawing once recovery finishes; save it under a new name.

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: Set to 0 to give RECOVER a command-line file prompt in a script.

parameters.name: AUDITCTL
parameters.description: 1 writes an .adt log of the recovery beside the file, which is worth keeping as evidence of what was repaired.

parameters.name: RECOVERYMODE
parameters.description: Controls whether drawing recovery information is recorded after a crash and whether the Recovery Manager opens automatically.

tools.example:
FILEDIA 0
AUDITCTL 1
RECOVER
C:/jobs/1042/1042-100.dwg
AUDIT
Y
-PURGE
All
*
N
SAVEAS

C:/jobs/1042/1042-100_RECOVERED.dwg
FILEDIA 1
tools.notes: Always recover to a new file name so the damaged original survives for a second attempt. RECOVERALL is the version to use when the xrefs are also suspect, because a corrupt xref can make a healthy host drawing appear broken. If RECOVER fails, try inserting the damaged file into a blank drawing with -INSERT, or opening the .bak or the .sv$ file that SAVETIME produced; DRAWINGRECOVERY lists all of those candidates after a crash.

tools.name: ETRANSMIT
tools.description: Package the current drawing together with everything it depends on - external references, raster images, PDF and DWF underlays, fonts, plot style tables, plotter configurations and sheet set data - into a single zip file, a folder, or a self-extracting executable. It is the correct way to send a drawing to anyone outside the office, because a bare DWG arrives with missing xrefs and substituted fonts. Transmittal setups store the options so the same package format can be produced every time.
tools.usage:
ETRANSMIT
(Create Transmittal dialog: Files Tree / Files Table, Transmittal Setups, View Report)
(Transmittal Setup: Transmittal package type - Folder | Self-extracting executable | Zip,
 File format, Transmittal file folder and name, Path options, Actions, Include options)

parameters.name: Transmittal package type
parameters.description: Folder of files, a self-extracting .exe, or a .zip. Zip is the usual choice for email and portals.

parameters.name: File format
parameters.description: Keep the existing DWG format or downsave every drawing in the package to an older release for the recipient.

parameters.name: Path options
parameters.description: Keep the folder hierarchy, place all files in one folder, or keep files and folders as they are. Flattening into one folder is what makes xrefs resolve on the recipient's machine.

parameters.name: Include fonts
parameters.description: Packs the SHX and TTF files the drawings use; without them the recipient sees substituted text.

parameters.name: Include textures / photometric web files / data link files
parameters.description: Additional dependencies for rendered models, lighting and Excel-linked tables.

parameters.name: Bind external references
parameters.description: Optionally bind or insert xrefs into the host drawings instead of shipping them separately.

parameters.name: Set default plotter to none / purge drawings
parameters.description: Actions applied to the packaged copies so they do not carry this office's device names or unused definitions.

tools.example:
; Issue a drawing package to a consultant
AUDIT
Y
-PURGE
All
*
N
QSAVE
ETRANSMIT
(Transmittal Setup: Zip, downsave to AutoCAD 2013, Path options = place all files in one folder,
 Include fonts, Set default plotter to none, transmittal file C:/issue/1042_ISSUE_C.zip)
tools.notes: Run View Report before creating the package: it lists any file AutoCAD could not find, which is the one thing a transmittal cannot fix for you. ETRANSMIT packages the drawing on disk, so save first - unsaved changes are not included unless the dialog is allowed to save. The Sheet Set Manager can create a transmittal for a whole sheet set in one operation; DWGCONVERT is the alternative when only the DWG version needs to change and the references are already local.

tools.name: DWGCONVERT
tools.description: Batch-convert a list of drawings to another DWG or DXF version, and optionally purge them, bind their xrefs, replace their plot style tables and repackage them, without opening each one. Conversion setups store the target format and options so the same conversion can be repeated for every issue. Use it when a client or a downstream system insists on a particular DWG release.
tools.usage:
DWGCONVERT
(Convert dialog: drawing list, Add File / Add Folder, Conversion Setups)
(Conversion Setup: Conversion package type - In-place | Folder | Self-extracting executable | Zip,
 File format, Path options, Actions - bind xrefs, purge drawings, replace page setups,
 Include options - fonts, textures, data link files)

parameters.name: drawing list
parameters.description: Built by adding files or whole folders, and saved as a .bp3 batch list so the same set can be converted again.

parameters.name: Conversion package type
parameters.description: In-place conversion overwrites the originals; Folder, Zip or self-extracting executable produce copies.

parameters.name: File format
parameters.description: The target DWG release, or DXF. This is the whole point of the command.

parameters.name: Bind external references
parameters.description: Bind or insert xrefs during conversion so each converted drawing is self-contained.

parameters.name: Purge drawings
parameters.description: Runs a purge on every converted drawing, which is the easiest way to clean a whole issue set.

parameters.name: Replace page setups
parameters.description: Swap in page setups from a chosen DWT so the converted sheets carry the recipient's plot settings.

parameters.name: Path options
parameters.description: Whether the folder structure is preserved or everything is flattened into one folder.

tools.example:
; Convert an issue folder to AutoCAD 2013 and purge on the way
DWGCONVERT
(Add Folder C:/jobs/1042/issue)
(Conversion Setup: package type Folder, file format AutoCAD 2013,
 Actions: purge drawings, bind external references,
 output folder C:/issue/2013)
(Convert)
tools.notes: In-place conversion has no undo - convert into a separate folder unless the originals are backed up. DWGCONVERT does not fix damaged files; run AUDIT or RECOVER on anything suspect first, because a corrupt drawing simply fails in the batch. ETRANSMIT is the right command when the goal is to send a package with its dependencies rather than to change format; SAVEAS handles a single file.

tools.name: XREF
tools.description: Manage external references: drawings, images, PDF, DWF, DGN and point cloud files that are displayed inside this drawing but stored separately. The command opens the External References palette, where references are attached, reloaded, unloaded, detached, bound and repathed, and where broken paths are spotted. The command-line form -XREF does all of the same operations without a dialog and is what scripts use.
tools.usage:
XREF  (alias XR; opens the External References palette, same as EXTERNALREFERENCES)

-XREF
Enter an option [?/Bind/Detach/Path/Unload/Reload/Overlay/Attach] <Attach>:
Enter external reference name(s): <name>

parameters.name: Attach (A) / Overlay (O)
parameters.description: Attach nests the reference when this drawing is itself referenced elsewhere; Overlay does not, which is how circular references are avoided.

parameters.name: Bind (B)
parameters.description: Make the reference a permanent part of this drawing. Bind renames dependent symbols to XREF$0$LAYER; the Insert option merges them as plain LAYER names.

parameters.name: Detach (D)
parameters.description: Remove the reference and all of its dependent named objects completely.

parameters.name: Unload (U) / Reload (R)
parameters.description: Unload keeps the link but stops loading the geometry, which speeds up a heavy drawing; Reload brings it back or picks up a colleague's changes.

parameters.name: Path (P)
parameters.description: Change the saved path of a reference. The palette also offers relative, full and no-path forms.

parameters.name: VISRETAIN
parameters.description: System variable: 1 keeps the layer colour, linetype and on/off settings you make for xref layers when the xref reloads.

parameters.name: XLOADCTL / PROJECTNAME
parameters.description: Demand loading of xref geometry, and the named search path used to find references whose saved path is wrong.

parameters.name: XREFOVERRIDE / XDWGFADECTL
parameters.description: Force xref objects to display ByLayer, and control how faded xrefs appear in the editor.

tools.example:
; Scripted repath and reload of every reference
FILEDIA 0
-XREF
P
SITE_SURVEY
C:/jobs/1042/survey/SITE_SURVEY.dwg
-XREF
R
*

; Bind one reference into the drawing before issue
-XREF
B
GRID
QSAVE
FILEDIA 1
tools.notes: EXTERNALREFERENCES opens exactly the same palette as XREF and is the name used on the ribbon; XREFPANEL and the older XBIND are separate commands. Relative paths survive moving a job folder, full paths do not - set them in the palette's Found At field. REFEDIT edits a reference in place from the host drawing, and XOPEN opens the referenced drawing in its own window, which is usually safer.

tools.name: XATTACH
tools.description: Attach a DWG file to the current drawing as an external reference, with a chosen insertion point, scale, rotation and path type. The referenced drawing stays a separate file, so changes made to it appear in every drawing that references it the next time they are opened or reloaded - which is what makes xrefs the backbone of team drafting. Reference Type decides whether the reference nests further up the chain.
tools.usage:
XATTACH  (alias XA)
(Select Reference File dialog, then Attach External Reference dialog)
  Reference Type: Attachment | Overlay
  Path type: Full path | Relative path | No path
  Insertion point / Scale / Rotation / Block Unit

; Scripted form
FILEDIA 0
-XREF
A
<xref name>
<full path to dwg>
Specify insertion point: 0,0
Enter X scale factor / Y scale factor / rotation angle:

parameters.name: Reference Type
parameters.description: Attachment nests when the host is itself referenced; Overlay is ignored one level up, which prevents circular references between team drawings.

parameters.name: Path type
parameters.description: Relative path is the safe default for a job folder that will be moved or transmitted; No path relies on the support search path and PROJECTNAME.

parameters.name: Insertion point
parameters.description: Normally 0,0,0 so that the reference lands on the host's origin and both drawings share a common coordinate system.

parameters.name: Scale / Rotation
parameters.description: Usually left at 1 and 0; scaling an xref makes dimensions and annotation inconsistent with the host.

parameters.name: Block Unit / INSUNITS
parameters.description: Units of the referenced drawing; a mismatch with the host's INSUNITS is the usual cause of an xref arriving 25.4 times too big.

parameters.name: Locate using Geographic Data
parameters.description: Positions the reference by its geographic location when both drawings carry geolocation data.

parameters.name: FILEDIA
parameters.description: Must be 0 for scripted attachment; use -XREF Attach rather than XATTACH in scripts.

tools.example:
; Attach the survey and the grid, then set the xref layer to non-plotting
FILEDIA 0
-XREF
A
SITE_SURVEY
C:/jobs/1042/survey/SITE_SURVEY.dwg
0,0
1
1
0
-XREF
O
GRID
C:/jobs/1042/GRID.dwg
0,0
1
1
0
FILEDIA 1

; AutoLISP
(command "_.-XREF" "_A" "SITE_SURVEY" "C:/jobs/1042/survey/SITE_SURVEY.dwg" '(0 0) 1 1 0)
tools.notes: Attach xrefs at 0,0,0 with scale 1 as a rule; anything else makes coordinates in the host and the reference disagree. Set VISRETAIN to 1 so layer settings made on xref layers survive a reload. XCLIP crops an attached reference to the area of interest, and ETRANSMIT is what collects the referenced files when the drawing leaves the office.

tools.name: XBIND
tools.description: Bind individual named objects from an external reference into the current drawing, rather than binding the whole reference. Blocks, dimension styles, layers, linetypes and text styles can each be pulled across on their own, which is how a standard detail block or a dimension style is adopted from a consultant's drawing without importing their entire model. Bound symbols are renamed from XREF|NAME to XREF$0$NAME.
tools.usage:
XBIND  (alias XB; dialog form)
(Xbind dialog: expand the xref, select Block, Dimstyle, Layer, Linetype or Textstyle, Add)

-XBIND
Enter symbol type to bind [Block/Dimstyle/LAyer/LType/Style]: B | D | LA | LT | S
Enter dependent <type> name(s): <XREFNAME|SYMBOLNAME>

parameters.name: Block
parameters.description: Bind one block definition from the reference so it can be inserted in the host drawing.

parameters.name: Dimstyle / Style
parameters.description: Bind a dimension style or a text style, which is the usual way to match a consultant's annotation.

parameters.name: LAyer / LType
parameters.description: Bind a layer definition or a linetype from the reference.

parameters.name: dependent name
parameters.description: Written as XREFNAME|SYMBOLNAME, for example GRID|COLUMN_MARK. The vertical bar is what marks a symbol as xref-dependent.

parameters.name: renaming
parameters.description: After binding, the symbol is called XREFNAME$0$SYMBOLNAME; the number increments if that name is already taken. RENAME tidies it afterwards.

tools.example:
; Adopt a block and a dimension style from an attached reference
-XBIND
B
GRID|COLUMN_MARK
-XBIND
D
GRID|ISO-25

; The block is now called GRID$0$COLUMN_MARK
RENAME
B
GRID$0$COLUMN_MARK
COLUMN_MARK
-INSERT
COLUMN_MARK
0,0
1
1
0
tools.notes: XBIND fails on a reference that is unloaded or on a symbol belonging to a nested xref - reload or bind the parent first. Binding a layer also brings in nothing else, so a bound block may still reference a layer that has to be bound separately. To bring the whole reference in permanently use -XREF Bind, whose Insert option merges symbol names without the $0$ prefix.

tools.name: XCLIP
tools.description: Crop an external reference or a block reference to a boundary so that only the part inside is displayed and plotted. The clip does not modify the referenced file - it is a property of the reference in this drawing and can be turned off, inverted or deleted at any time. Clipping large site or model xrefs to the area a sheet actually shows is the single most effective way to speed up a heavy drawing.
tools.usage:
XCLIP  (alias XC)
Select objects: <xref or block reference>
Enter clipping option [ON/OFF/Clipdepth/Delete/generate Polyline/Invert clip/New boundary] <New>:
Specify clipping boundary or select invert option:
[Select polyline/Polygonal/Rectangular/Invert clip] <Rectangular>:

parameters.name: New boundary (N)
parameters.description: Create the clip from a rectangle, a polygon drawn now, or an existing closed polyline.

parameters.name: ON / OFF
parameters.description: Suspend the clip without losing the boundary, and restore it. Useful when checking what has been cropped away.

parameters.name: Invert clip (I)
parameters.description: Hide what is inside the boundary instead of outside - the way a hole is punched through a reference.

parameters.name: Delete (D)
parameters.description: Remove the boundary altogether and show the whole reference again. ERASE does not remove a clip boundary.

parameters.name: generate Polyline (P)
parameters.description: Draw a polyline on top of the existing clip boundary so it can be edited and reapplied.

parameters.name: Clipdepth (C)
parameters.description: Set front and back clipping planes on a 3D reference so only a slab of the model is shown.

parameters.name: XCLIPFRAME
parameters.description: 0 the boundary is not displayed or plotted, 1 displayed and plotted, 2 displayed but not plotted - the usual production setting.

parameters.name: FRAME
parameters.description: Master system variable that overrides XCLIPFRAME, IMAGEFRAME, PDFFRAME, DWFFRAME, DGNFRAME and WIPEOUTFRAME in one go.

tools.example:
; Clip the site xref to the area shown on this sheet, frame visible but not plotted
XCLIP
(select the SITE_SURVEY xref)

N
R
12000,4000
28000,16000
XCLIPFRAME
2
REGEN

; Punch a hole through a reference
XCLIP
(select the xref)

N
I
P
(pick the polygon vertices)
tools.notes: IMAGECLIP, PDFCLIP, DWFCLIP and DGNCLIP do the same job for raster images and the various underlay types, with the same New/ON/OFF/Delete options. Set FRAME to 2 once to make every reference frame visible on screen but absent from output. A clipped xref still loads its whole file unless demand loading is on - set XLOADCTL to 2 for the biggest speed gain on clipped references.

tools.name: IMAGEATTACH
tools.description: Attach a raster image - aerial photograph, scanned drawing, logo, site photo - as a reference in the current drawing. Like a DWG xref the image file stays external and is only linked, so the DWG stays small and the picture updates if the file is replaced. Scale, rotation and insertion point are set at attachment, and the image can then be cropped, faded and pushed behind the drawing.
tools.usage:
IMAGEATTACH  (alias IAT)
(Select Image File dialog, then Attach Image dialog)
  Path type: Full path | Relative path | No path
  Insertion point / Scale / Rotation

; Related commands
IMAGECLIP    crop the attached image
IMAGEADJUST  brightness, contrast and fade
IMAGEQUALITY draft or high display quality
TRANSPARENCY treat the image background as transparent

parameters.name: Path type
parameters.description: Relative path keeps the link working when the job folder moves; images are a frequent cause of broken links after archiving.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: The image has no real-world size of its own unless a world file accompanies it, so scale it against known geometry after attaching.

parameters.name: IMAGEFRAME
parameters.description: 0 frame hidden and not plotted, 1 displayed and plotted, 2 displayed but not plotted. FRAME overrides it along with all the other reference frames.

parameters.name: IMAGEADJUST
parameters.description: Brightness, contrast and fade of an attached image; fading a scanned background to about 50 per cent keeps new work readable.

parameters.name: IMAGEQUALITY
parameters.description: Draft or High display quality. Draft redraws much faster on large aerials and does not affect plotted output.

parameters.name: DRAWORDER
parameters.description: Almost always needed after attaching, to send the image behind the drawing.

parameters.name: TRANSPARENCY
parameters.description: Makes the background of a bitonal image transparent so geometry behind it shows through.

tools.example:
; Attach and scale an aerial, then push it behind everything
IMAGEATTACH
(select C:/jobs/1042/survey/aerial.tif, relative path, insertion 0,0, scale 1)
SCALE
L

0,0
R
0,0
100,0
(pick the matching known distance)
DRAWORDER
L

B
IMAGEFRAME
2
IMAGEADJUST
L

(fade 50)
tools.notes: IMAGECLIP crops an attached image with the same New/ON/OFF/Delete options as XCLIP, and IMAGEFRAME 2 is the usual production setting so the border shows on screen but not on paper. The External References palette (XREF) manages images, PDF, DWF and DGN underlays alongside DWG references, including reloading and repathing them. ETRANSMIT packages linked images; a drawing sent without them arrives with empty frames.

tools.name: PDFATTACH
tools.description: Attach one page of a PDF file as an underlay: a linked, non-editable backdrop that can be snapped to, clipped, faded and layered. Object snaps work against the PDF's vector geometry when PDFOSNAP is on, which makes it practical to trace or measure over a consultant's drawing without converting anything. The file stays external, so the PDF can be replaced and the drawing updates.
tools.usage:
PDFATTACH
(Select PDF File dialog, then Attach PDF Underlay dialog)
  Page: select one page of the PDF
  Path type: Full path | Relative path | No path
  Insertion point / Scale / Rotation

; Related commands
PDFCLIP    crop the underlay
PDFLAYERS  show or hide layers stored in the PDF
PDFADJUST  contrast, fade, monochrome display

parameters.name: Page
parameters.description: One page per attachment; a multi-page set needs one PDFATTACH per page.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: The underlay arrives at PDF page size, so it normally has to be scaled against a known dimension after attaching.

parameters.name: PDFOSNAP
parameters.description: System variable: 1 enables object snapping to the vector geometry inside the underlay, which is what makes tracing accurate.

parameters.name: PDFFRAME
parameters.description: 0 frame hidden and not plotted, 1 displayed and plotted, 2 displayed but not plotted; FRAME overrides it.

parameters.name: PDFADJUST
parameters.description: Contrast, fade and monochrome display of the underlay; fading it makes new work stand out.

parameters.name: PDFLAYERS
parameters.description: Switches individual layers stored in a layered PDF on and off.

parameters.name: Path type
parameters.description: Relative path for job folders that move; the underlay shows an empty frame when the path breaks.

tools.example:
; Attach a consultant's PDF, scale it to a known dimension and trace over it
PDFATTACH
(select C:/incoming/STRUCT-100.pdf, page 1, relative path, insertion 0,0, scale 1)
PDFOSNAP
1
SCALE
L

0,0
R
(pick the two ends of a dimensioned line)
(type the true length)
PDFADJUST
L

(fade 60)
PDFFRAME
2
tools.notes: An underlay is a picture with snappable vectors, not AutoCAD objects - use PDFIMPORT when the geometry itself is needed. DWFATTACH, DGNATTACH and POINTCLOUDATTACH work the same way for DWF, MicroStation and scanned point cloud data, each with matching CLIP, ADJUST and FRAME commands and variables. Underlays are managed in the External References palette alongside DWG xrefs and images.

tools.name: PDFIMPORT
tools.description: Convert the contents of a PDF page into real AutoCAD objects: vector geometry becomes lines, polylines and splines, solid fills become hatches or 2D solids, TrueType text becomes text objects and raster images are extracted to files and attached. It works either on an attached PDF underlay or straight from a file, and the imported area can be the whole page or a picked region. It is the practical answer to receiving a drawing as a PDF and needing to work on it.
tools.usage:
PDFIMPORT
Select PDF underlay or [File] <File>: <select an underlay> | F
(when importing from a file, the Import PDF dialog appears)
  Page to import / Location / Scale / Rotation
  PDF data to import: Vector geometry, Solid fills, TrueType text, Raster images
  Layers: Use PDF layers | Create object layers | Current layer
  Import options: Import as block, Join line and arc segments,
                  Convert solid fills to hatches, Apply lineweight properties, Infer linetypes

parameters.name: Vector geometry
parameters.description: Lines, arcs and curves become AutoCAD objects. Join line and arc segments merges the fragments a PDF writer produces into sensible polylines.

parameters.name: Solid fills
parameters.description: Converted to 2D solids, or to hatches when Convert solid fills to hatches is on.

parameters.name: TrueType text
parameters.description: Comes in as editable text. SHX text in a PDF is only geometry and arrives as lines unless PDFSHXTEXT recognises it afterwards.

parameters.name: Raster images
parameters.description: Extracted to image files in the folder named by PDFIMPORTIMAGEPATH and attached as image references.

parameters.name: Layers
parameters.description: Use the PDF's own layers, create layers named after the PDF object types, or dump everything on the current layer. PDFIMPORTLAYERS holds the setting.

parameters.name: Import as block
parameters.description: Wraps the whole import in a single block reference, which keeps the drawing tidy and easy to erase in one go.

parameters.name: PDFIMPORTFILTER
parameters.description: Bit-coded system variable choosing which data types are imported - vectors, solid fills, text, images.

parameters.name: Infer linetypes
parameters.description: Recognises dashed patterns in the PDF and applies AutoCAD linetypes instead of importing hundreds of short segments.

tools.example:
; Attach, check, then import the vectors as a block
PDFATTACH
(select C:/incoming/STRUCT-100.pdf, page 1, insertion 0,0, scale 1)
PDFIMPORT
(select the underlay)
(Import as block: on, Join line and arc segments: on,
 Convert solid fills to hatches: on, Layers: Use PDF layers)

; Turn imported SHX line work back into text
PDFSHXTEXT
(select the imported geometry)

SCALE
(scale the result to true size if the PDF was not plotted 1:1)
tools.notes: A PDF produced by plotting at 1:100 imports at paper size, so the result nearly always needs scaling and a good look at line weights. SHX fonts carry no character information in a PDF: PDFSHXTEXT recognises the geometry and replaces it with text objects, with an accuracy that depends on the font. PDFIMPORT creates a lot of small objects - run OVERKILL and PURGE afterwards, and expect to rebuild dimensions and hatches by hand.

tools.name: DATAEXTRACTION
tools.description: Extract properties and block attribute values from the objects in one or more drawings, or a whole sheet set, and output them as a table in the drawing, an external CSV, XLS, MDB or TXT file, or both. The wizard walks through choosing the data source, filtering which objects and properties are wanted, sorting and combining rows, and adding a count column. The definition is saved as a .dxe file so the same schedule can be regenerated whenever the drawing changes.
tools.usage:
DATAEXTRACTION  (alias DX)
(Data Extraction wizard, eight pages)
  1 Begin: create a new extraction (.dxe) or edit an existing one
  2 Define Data Source: drawings, folders or the current sheet set; include xrefs and blocks
  3 Select Objects: which block and object types to extract
  4 Select Properties: which properties and attribute tags, by category
  5 Refine Data: sort, reorder, combine identical rows, add count and name columns
  6 Choose Output: table in the drawing and/or external file
  7 Table Style
  8 Finish

parameters.name: Data source
parameters.description: The current drawing, a list of drawings, whole folders, or the current sheet set. Extraction across a folder is how a project-wide schedule is built.

parameters.name: Include xrefs / nested blocks
parameters.description: Decides whether objects inside references and nested blocks are counted; leaving xrefs in usually doubles the count unexpectedly.

parameters.name: Properties
parameters.description: Grouped by category - Attribute, Geometry, General, Drawing, 3D Visualization. Attribute tags defined with ATTDEF appear here by name.

parameters.name: Combine identical rows / Show count column
parameters.description: Turns a list of every insertion into a quantity schedule.

parameters.name: Output: table
parameters.description: Inserts a table object linked to the extraction, formatted by a chosen table style.

parameters.name: Output: external file
parameters.description: Writes .csv, .xls, .mdb or .txt for use in a spreadsheet or a purchasing system.

parameters.name: .dxe file
parameters.description: The saved extraction definition - source, filters, properties and formatting - so the schedule can be rebuilt after the drawing changes.

parameters.name: DXEVAL
parameters.description: Bit-coded system variable controlling when extraction tables and fields are automatically updated, for example on open, save or plot.

tools.example:
; Build a valve schedule from attributed blocks
DATAEXTRACTION
(New extraction -> C:/jobs/1042/schedules/valves.dxe)
(Data source: current drawing, include blocks in xrefs: off)
(Objects: VALVE_GATE, VALVE_BALL)
(Properties: TAG_NO, SIZE, RATING, plus Count)
(Refine: combine identical rows, show count column)
(Output: insert data extraction table into drawing and write C:/jobs/1042/schedules/valves.csv)

; Refresh after editing the drawing
-DATAEXTRACTION or reselect the table and use Update Table Data Links
tools.notes: For a scriptable attribute dump, the legacy -ATTEXT command extracts block attributes using a .txt template into CDF, SDF or DXF format without a wizard; EATTEXT simply launches DATAEXTRACTION in current releases. An extraction table inserted in the drawing updates from its .dxe definition, not live from the objects, so it must be refreshed after changes. DATALINK is the opposite direction - data coming in from a spreadsheet.

tools.name: DATALINK
tools.description: Create and manage links between an AutoCAD table and a range in a Microsoft Excel file, so that schedules, door lists and quantities live in the spreadsheet and the drawing shows them. A link can be to a whole sheet, a named range or a cell range, and it can be one-way into the drawing or two-way so edits in the table are written back. DATALINKUPDATE performs the update in either direction.
tools.usage:
DATALINK  (alias DL)
(Data Link Manager: Create a new Excel Data Link, Edit, Rename, Delete)
(New Excel Data Link dialog: file path, Link entire sheet | Link to a named range | Link to range,
 Cell contents: keep data formats and formulas | keep data formats, solve formulas in AutoCAD |
 convert to AutoCAD entities, Allow writing to source file)

; Then
TABLE  -> From a data link
DATALINKUPDATE  update the table from the file, or the file from the table

parameters.name: Link entire sheet / named range / range
parameters.description: How much of the workbook the table shows. A named range is the robust choice because inserted rows do not break it.

parameters.name: Cell contents
parameters.description: Keep Excel formatting and formulas, keep formatting but recalculate in AutoCAD, or convert the values to plain AutoCAD content.

parameters.name: Allow writing to source file
parameters.description: Enables two-way editing, so DATALINKUPDATE can push changes from the AutoCAD table back into the spreadsheet.

parameters.name: DATALINKUPDATE
parameters.description: Updates the data link; its options choose the direction (update table from source, or write data to source).

parameters.name: DATALINKNOTIFY
parameters.description: System variable controlling whether the balloon notification appears when a linked file has changed.

parameters.name: Link lock
parameters.description: Locked cells in a linked table cannot be edited in AutoCAD; unlock them before trying to write back.

tools.example:
; Bring a door schedule in from Excel
DATALINK
(Create a new Excel Data Link -> name DOOR_SCHEDULE)
(File C:/jobs/1042/schedules/doors.xlsx, Link to named range DOORS,
 keep data formats and formulas, Allow writing to source file: on)

TABLE
(Insert options: From a data link -> DOOR_SCHEDULE)
200,150

; After the spreadsheet is revised
DATALINKUPDATE
(update the table from the source file)
tools.notes: Excel must be installed for a data link to be created or updated, and the workbook must not be open exclusively by another user. Fields in text can reference a linked table's cells, so a note can quote a quantity that the spreadsheet controls. OLELINKS manages older OLE-embedded objects and is the legacy alternative; DATAEXTRACTION is the right tool when the data comes from the drawing rather than from a spreadsheet.
